summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, status post failed kidney transplant, coronary artery disease, and chronic interstitial lung disease, was admitted with fever and substernal chest pain radiating to the chin following a dialysis session. He was febrile in the emergency department but had no focal infection signs. A CT chest showed stable chronic interstitial lung disease without pneumonia but revealed pulmonary arterial dilation suggestive of pulmonary hypertension. Blood cultures were negative, and he did not spike a fever during admission. Chest pain was consistent with chronic angina, with no troponin rise or EKG changes to suggest acute myocardial infarction. He continued his home cardiac and renal medications, completed a scheduled hemodialysis session, and remained stable. He was discharged home with instructions to follow up with his cardiologist for a planned procedure and to monitor for recurrent symptoms.
problems: Chronic total occlusion of coronary artery
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
